points.label: Action and response
points.left: Ruth’s closing movement joins birth, neighborhood naming, Obed, Jesse, and David in one family line.
points.right: Samuel comes to Bethlehem, Jesse’s sons pass before him, David is fetched from the sheep, and the spirit rushes on him after anointing.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David appears as the final named descendant inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the youngest son is selected and the spirit comes on him inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Ruth 4:13–22 and 1 Samuel 16:1–13 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Ancestry, Anointing, and Court” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.
payload.tension: Ruth 4:13–22 foregrounds David appears as the final named descendant; 1 Samuel 16:1–13 foregrounds the youngest son is selected and the spirit comes on him. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
payload.title: A Bethlehem genealogy reaches David / Chosen outside the expected lineup
